note: THE OFFER LEDGER: four core offers, seven selectable configurations, one source of truth. Prices live here and nowhere else. Values marked approved:true render as real prices. Values marked approved:false NEVER render a number to a visitor; they render the offer's public_note instead, in polished language, with no warning chip, no filename, no branch name and no developer reasoning. Internal reasoning belongs in docs/sales-redesign/, never on the page. Derived values (Equity base, Equity cap, Runway first-year) are computed by js/offers.js from the formulas below and must never be hardcoded.
estimate_disclaimer: This is an estimate, not the final agreement.

equity_cap.note: The cap is never a stored constant. It is the multiplier times the normal twelve-month value of the service at its approved standard price.

runway_year_start.note: Going live with the year paid: the domain plus the twelve months. The monthly path's $66 buys the domain and month one only.

equity.name: Equity Uprise
equity.short: A lower monthly price, and a time-limited share of eligible connected revenue.

eligibility.note: WHAT MAKES SOMEBODY ELIGIBLE, and why each one is not negotiable. Equity Uprise is paid out of a share of revenue, so the whole arrangement rests on that revenue being measurable. Every requirement below exists to make it measurable; none of them is a preference.

requirements.must: The website has to be one we built.
requirements.why: The revenue share is calculated from what the site brings in. On a site somebody else built and hosts, we cannot see the orders, cannot verify a total, and would be asking the customer to self-report the number their own bill is based on. That is not a term either side should accept.

requirements.must: The connected traffic has to run through that website.
requirements.why: A link in a bio that goes straight to a third-party checkout is a sale the site never sees. The share is on CONNECTED revenue, and traffic routed around the site is revenue nobody can connect - which ends in an argument about a number instead of a business getting built.

requirements.must: Payments have to run on the rails we connect for you.
requirements.why: This is the meter. It is what turns 'eligible connected revenue' from a phrase in an agreement into a figure both sides can read off the same screen on the same day.

eligibility.plain: To qualify: the website is one we built, your traffic runs through it, and payments run on the rails we connect. That is what makes the revenue countable, and the whole arrangement is priced off a count.
eligibility.not_eligible: A business that wants to keep its existing site, or send its buyers somewhere else to pay, can still work with us - at the standard price, with no revenue share and nothing to measure. That is M Mode, and it is not a lesser door.

equity.plain: No stock. No membership interest. No ownership. Equity Uprise is a time-limited revenue-share agreement. Revenue sharing ends at the earlier of the stated term or the stated cap, whichever comes first. The domain is always paid separately, up front. Participation requires a program-fit review and a signed agreement.
equity.acknowledgement: I understand Equity Uprise shares a percentage of eligible connected revenue for a limited term, that it takes no ownership of my business, and that the final terms are set in a signed agreement.

revenue_definition.working_basis: Eligible online revenue processed through the connected payment rails used by the website.
revenue_definition.public_note: What counts as eligible revenue, how it is measured and how it is reported are set with you in discovery and written into the agreement before anything is signed.

offers.name: Domain and hosting
offers.infrastructure_note: This is not the fourth service. It is the ground the other three stand on, and it is priced like plumbing rather than like work.
offers.tagline: Icons in the clique. Stop scrolls of death.
offers.lede: The runway your business takes off from, and here is what the runway actually is. The domain is your address: yourname.com, rented a year at a time, and it is yours, not a slug hanging off somebody else's platform. The hosting is the ground it sits on: the machine that answers when somebody types that address, kept online, kept secure, kept backed up. Two bills, both mine to run. The website itself I build for free.
offers.equity_note: Domain and hosting has no Equity Uprise version. There is no reason to trade a share of your revenue for an address and a machine to keep it online.

deposit.label: to start the draft
deposit.line: Sends the work before the domain. The draft gets built and previewed first, and the $33 is your first month, not an extra fee. It is also the first of the drafts: buying the domain puts you on a draft a month.

recurring.label: hosting, every month after the first

annual.label: to go live, year of hosting paid
annual.note: The same service. Paying the twelve months together drops the monthly rate from $33 to $30.

drafts.name: A draft a month
drafts.headline: Buying the domain puts you on a redraw.
drafts.what: A draft is a fresh cut of your site: new work on the layout, the copy, the photography, whatever the last month showed was not landing. Not a support ticket and not a patch. A draft, made for you, that you either take or leave standing.

first_year.line: Twelve months, twelve drafts. One a month for the first year, starting with the one the deposit paid for.

after.line: After the first year it settles to a draft every quarter, and it never stops. Four a year, for as long as the site is hosted here, at no extra charge.

upgraded.line: On the full management service it never steps down. A draft a month, for as long as the service runs.

drafts.plain: Nobody else gives you a redesign every month for the price of hosting. That is the whole point: the site is never the one you bought a year ago.

offers.revenue_share_line: None. You keep 100% of what you make.

replaces.internal_note: Domain and hosting replaces the $87/mo Hosting plan for all new customers. The $87 plan is preserved in legacy_plans for grandfathered agreements and existing records. It must not appear in the active new-customer journey.

activation.name: The first month
activation.free_note: The whole management service, every module, for one month at no charge. Not a trial of a cut-down version: the real thing, running.
activation.shape: One module a week. Each one is switched on, working, and producing something you can look at before the next one starts, so by the end of the month you have watched every part of it earn its place instead of being handed a bundle and a bill.

sprints.name: The website goes up
sprints.what: Build, content, domain pointed, live and indexed. The room everything else sends people to.
sprints.after: yours. It does not switch off, whatever you decide at the end of the month.

sprints.name: Inbound turned on
sprints.what: Automation built into your own backend that works on the traffic coming toward you: search surface, the paths people already take to find somebody doing what you do, and capture at the end of every one of them so an arrival becomes a name and a number.
sprints.after: at the end of the free month unless the service continues, and everything it built stays on the record.

sprints.name: Outbound turned on
sprints.what: The other direction: automated reach-out and follow-up running from the same backend, so the people worth contacting get contacted and nobody goes cold because a week got busy.
sprints.after: at the end of the free month unless the service continues, and everything it built stays on the record.

sprints.name: Social activated
sprints.what: Those same tools pointed at your feeds. Scheduling, posting and the parts of being present online that eat an evening, running without you sitting in them.
sprints.after: at the end of the free month unless the service continues, and everything it built stays on the record.

at_the_end.prompt: At the end of the month you decide, once, with a month of evidence instead of a pitch.

options.name: Keep it
options.what: Everything stays exactly as it is running. The standard price starts from that month.

options.name: Keep social, on Equity
options.what: The social module alone stays running, on Equity Uprise: a lower monthly price against a capped, time-limited share of eligible connected revenue. No ownership is taken, and it needs a program-fit review and a signed agreement, so it is arranged rather than clicked.

options.name: Cruise
options.what: The three automation modules switch off. The website stays live, stays indexed and stays yours, and you are back to the address and the machine that keeps it online.

at_the_end.no_trap: There is no notice period, no cancellation fee, and nothing to phone up and argue about. Cruising is a button, not a negotiation, and the site does not go dark when you press it.

customer_license.name: The customer licence
customer_license.headline: Every customer gets the catalogue.
customer_license.lede: The music is not an upsell here. Anybody on a management service can use the McCluster catalogue in their own business, at no charge, for as long as the service is running. Not a stock-library subscription and not a royalty-free clip: the actual records, licensed from the artist who made them.
customer_license.granted_note: It comes with the management service, in either mode. Equity Uprise customers get exactly the same grant as M Mode customers.
customer_license.term: For as long as the service is running.
customer_license.ends: The licence runs with the subscription. Stop the service and the grant stops with it, which is the only honest way to give something away: it is a reason to stay, not a hostage. Anything already published stays published; you simply do not add new uses after that.

covers.name: On your website
covers.what: The catalogue playing on your own site. Background beds, a hero film, a landing page that opens with a record instead of silence.

covers.name: In your store
covers.what: Played in your place of business. A shop, a studio, a salon, a restaurant floor: the room can run the record all day.

covers.name: Under your posts
covers.what: Your own social content, on your own accounts, scored with the catalogue. The reels the management service is already making for you land pre-cleared.

covers.name: The swag, in your store
covers.public_note: Stocking and selling McCluster merchandise from your storefront is on the table for customers with a physical location. Which pieces, what the split is and how they are supplied are set with you and written into the agreement.

excludes: Reselling or sublicensing the music to anybody else
Broadcast, cinema and paid media placements, which are quoted on their own
Anything that puts the recording in a product you sell as a product
customer_license.delivery: The files land by email when the service starts: the records themselves, and the written grant naming what you can do with them.
customer_license.still_a_desk: Everybody else licenses the same catalogue the ordinary way, and that desk has not moved.
